create 1,000 rows: tie with Octane, Vue 3 and Vapor in both runs
replace all rows: tie with Octane, Vapor and Vue 3 in both runs
partial update: tie with Vapor and Octane in both runs
select row: below clock resolution here; batch-timed on the same board, Pyreon is 1.49–1.50× faster than Octane (both runs)
swap rows: Vapor 1.07× ahead in run 1, a tie in run 2, so not claimed either way
remove row: tie with Octane, Vapor and Solid 2.0 in both runs
clear rows: tie in run 1, a 1.12× win in run 2: not claimed · batch-timed, Octane 1.02× ahead (both runs)
create 10,000 rows: tie with Vapor, Vue 3 and Octane in both runs · 2.7× faster than React 19, 3.9× than Preact (run 1 figures)
append 1k → 10k: tie with Octane in both runs

losses: Memory per component

A mounted 2,047-component tree retains 355 KB in Pyreon against 206–207 KB in Solid 1.9, 1.72× (both runs, no CI); Pyreon is below Solid 2.0's 411 KB. On the row board Pyreon and Preact are level (3.15–3.16 vs 3.15 MB), not lighter.
A keyed list with conditional cells

A plain .map() of JSX rows loses create (1.07–1.08×) and replace (1.03–1.04×). With <For> both split between runs: a 1.02–1.03× loss in run 1, a tie in run 2. Clearing 1,000 rows is a win with either.
Most of the row board is a tie

Create 1,000, replace, partial update, remove, create 10,000 and append tie Vue 3.6 Vapor, Octane and Vue 3. Clear rows and swap split between runs; swap was a 1.07× loss to Vapor in one. The batch-timed clear cycle is a 1.02× loss to Octane in both runs. The batch-timed select is our one outright win.
Deep-tree mount, one run of two
A tie with Solid 1.9 in run 1; Solid 1.9 1.05× ahead in run 2, so a split, not claimed. It tied in both runs on 2026-11-24. Solid 2.0 and React are slower in both runs.
Swap at 100 and 1,000 rows
Octane leads 1.12× and 1.10× on the batch instrument (one run, 2026-11-05), a result that moves with batch size. We report it as a loss.
Hydrating a 1,000-row table
Tied with Vue 3 on the framework walk in both runs. On the total, tied in run 1 and Vue 1.01× ahead in run 2.
Charts line mounts, row input
10,000 points: uPlot 1.17–1.20×. 1,000,000 points: Chart.js 1.16–1.20×. Columnar input ties, except a 1.18× loss to uPlot at 10,000 points in run 1.
Signal creation
About 5× slower than Preact Signals on both engines. Deep unobserved chains lose too (1.42–1.43× on V8, 1.15–1.21× on JavaScriptCore), and so does wide fan-out on V8 (1.03–1.04×).
Bundle size
18.5 KB for the same app. Solid ships 7.7 KB, Preact 10.1 KB, Svelte 16.1 KB.
Small route tables

Hono matches 10 routes 1.91× faster (one run). Per row, Pyreon trails the fastest router on static, nested-static, dynamic, nested-dynamic and splat matches at every size. The harness changed after these figures (PR #4142: Hono's arm now builds its params object like every other arm), so the next run will move them.
Store setup and reads

The record lists store setup and store reads as losses to Zustand. The harness changed after those figures (PR #4142: the setup op no longer builds a store id inside the timed loop), so we don't quote them until the next quiet-machine run replaces them.
Six validator cells
Zod's compiled mode wins valid email, int and array-of-20 parses; ArkType wins the valid user-object parse. On checks, typia and ArkType win valid email and ArkType wins invalid email. One run.
A few nanoseconds and kilobytes
Storage reads (1.5×), url-state integer parse (1.1×), form heap (Solid modular-forms 0.09 MB lighter), code editor bundle (4%).
Happy-dom table and list rows

Under happy-dom (not a browser), table mount at 1,000 rows, single-cell update vs memoized rows at 1,000 and sort vs memoized rows at 100 lose to react-table, and virtual's 10,000-row mount loses 1.1×. In real Chromium the table mount ties in one run and wins 1.03× in the other, and virtual mounts 1.15× faster (one run).
Unbundled Node
A process that imports the built package without a bundler pays a live process.env read per dev check, about 145 ns each on V8. Every bundler folds it away.
withdrawn: "Solid mounts a deep component tree 1.15–1.18× faster"
Gone since #4199 (static component props folded at compile time), bisected. On 2026-11-25 the mount splits with Solid 1.9: a tie in run 1, Solid 1.9 1.05× in run 2. Its memory is still a loss.
"Pyreon ties Preact as the lightest framework"
Not claimed. After the row board Pyreon reads 3.15–3.16 MB and Preact 3.15 MB (2026-11-25): level at 0.01 MB, with no confidence interval.
"Solid wins effect-list dispose by one clock quantum"
Every close arm reads 35–50 µs, under 10 clock quanta, so it gets no verdict.
"~4.9× partial update lead over Solid"
A table-layout harness bug inflated it. Re-measured at about 2.1×; today Pyreon is 1.90–1.98× faster than Solid 1.9 and 2.0 on partial update.
"Pyreon wins clear rows outright, 1.12×"
Published on 2026-11-24 from two winning runs. On 2026-11-25 run 1 tied Octane and run 2 won 1.12×, so it is a split and not claimed.
"Pyreon outright on create 1,000 / replace all / create 10,000"
Create 1,000, replace all and create 10,000 tie in both runs.
"Append 1k → 10k: Pyreon wins 1.02×"
Page-load-aware intervals turned it into a split, and the 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-25 runs tie in both. Not claimed.
"Vue 3.6 Vapor outright on replace all (1.02×) and swap rows (1.08×)"
Ties in both runs. Withdrawn for them too.
"Fastest framework"
Never as a bare claim. Most of the row board is a tie; we name the operation and the margin.
"Pyreon has the lowest retained heap" (forms)
Solid modular-forms is lighter, 2.33 vs 2.42 MB.
"Fastest median on dbmon"
A three-way tie in both runs. dbmon is never a win for anyone.
"cssVariables theming 1.16× / 1.22× faster"
Reversed: classic mode is 1.13× faster.
"react-table mounts 1.12–1.13× faster"
Didn't reproduce on the current build: a tie in run 1, Pyreon 1.03× in run 2.
"Preact wins the computed diamond" (1.13× V8, 1.01× JavaScriptCore)
Pyreon now wins it in both runs: 1.30–1.31× on V8, 1.07–1.08× on JavaScriptCore.
"zod wins invalid scalar string 1.17×"
Pyreon leads that cell now, 1.40× vs zod (one run, the weakest of twelve).
runtime-server throughput of 2026-09-24
Not comparable: the harness was re-added after that run (#3642).
Any figure older than 2026-11-05
This record supersedes every earlier run. Sections a later run did not re-measure keep their figures and their date: row board and core scenarios 2026-11-25, bundle 2026-11-24, the rest 2026-11-05.
method: Every suite runs alone, gated on a machine load below 4, with load stamped before and after.
Every implementation must produce the same observable result before a single timing counts.
Medians with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals that resample whole page loads, not just samples.
A win needs non-overlapping intervals in every run. Overlap is a tie, not "basically faster". A result measured once says "one run".
NODE_ENV=production and a real vite build for every browser suite, cross-origin isolated for a 5 µs clock.
We wrote these benchmarks and we judge them, on one machine, in Chromium only. A keyed implementation is staged for krausest/js-framework-benchmark, the independent venue (not yet submitted).

lossesSection.title: Every loss, in one list.
lossesSection.intro: Wins lead this page. Everything else is here too: every loss from §13 of the record, in one list. We publish where we lose, so you can trust where we win.

harnessBugs.title: Eight bugs we found in our own benchmarks.
harnessBugs.intro: Each one was found, fixed, re-run and published, and each now has a guard that stops it. Where a bug flattered us, the claim came down.

items.title: Rivals on slow paths
items.text: Svelte and Vue arms ran on deep proxies and Octane was pinned eight patches behind; the Svelte create-10,000 gap fell from about 2.5× to 1.19× once fixed. Guard: every arm on its framework's documented fast path, compiler-output arms diffed against the real toolchain's emit.

items.title: A 100 µs clock
items.text: Chromium clamps performance.now() on a non-isolated page, so sub-millisecond ops reported clock ticks: "Octane 2.00× ahead" on clear rows was 1.19–1.45×. Guard: cross-origin-isolated pages with a measured 5 µs quantum (the harness aborts otherwise) and a batch instrument for ops under about 10 quanta.

items.title: A String() wrapper
items.text: String(row.id) switched off Octane's compiler fast path and taxed four Octane ops. Guard: no presentation work a real user would not write, and competitor arms are checked by compiling them.

items.title: A V8 string cache
items.text: Growth of V8's number-to-string cache was billed to the retained heap of the five arms that stringified ids. Guard: every arm renders the raw row.id, and a heap-diff script checks GC-root-held entries.

items.title: table-layout: auto
items.text: Whole-table re-measures made append bimodal and inflated a Pyreon partial-update lead about 2.3× (published as ~4.9×, now withdrawn). Guard: table-layout: fixed for every arm plus a bimodality guard.

items.title: A busy machine
items.text: A hydration "tie" with Vue was measured at load 8.2; on a quiet machine Vue led by 3–4%. Guard: strictly sequential runs gated on a one-minute load below 4, and a close verdict needs two agreeing runs.

items.title: A rival's upgrade
items.text: A ~3.1× clear-rows swing was about 1.5× Pyreon getting faster and about 3× Octane 0.2.2 getting slower. Guard: split "Pyreon moved" from "competitor moved" before explaining a change, and never call a gap architectural.

items.title: Pooled intervals
items.text: 100 samples from 5 page loads were bootstrapped as if independent. Guard: a two-stage cluster bootstrap over page loads; fewer than three page loads prints "verdicts provisional". It turned two pooled wins (create 10,000, append) into splits.

reproduce.title: Don't trust us. Run it.
reproduce.intro: Every suite is in the repository. Clone it, install, and the row board runs in real Chromium on your machine. Absolute times depend on the machine; compare ratios.
reproduce.command:
git clone https://github.com/pyreon/pyreon
cd pyreon && bun install && bunx playwright install chromium
cd examples/benchmark && bun bench-fair.ts --repeat 5 --wait-quiet 4
reproduce.allSuites:
cd examples/benchmark
bun bench-fair.ts --repeat 5 --wait-quiet 4
bun bench-scenarios.ts --scenario <dbmon|tree|effects|memo> --repeat 5 --wait-quiet 4
bun bench-scenarios.ts --scenario <flow|table|virtual|charts|charts-libs> --repeat 3 --wait-quiet 4
bun bench-hydration.ts --repeat 5 --wait-quiet 4 && bun bench-apppage.ts --repeat 3 --wait-quiet 4
bun bench-crossover.ts --repeat 3
bun bench-bundle.ts
bun bench-ssr.ts --wait-quiet 4 && bun bench-charts-bundle.ts
cd ../.. && bun scripts/bench/core/reactivity.ts && bun scripts/bench/core/reactivity.ts --runtime node
bun scripts/bench/core/router.ts && bun scripts/bench/core/validate.ts

# any fundamentals package
cd packages/fundamentals/<pkg> && NODE_ENV=production bun bench/<file>.ts
reproduce.note: --wait-quiet 4 waits until the machine's one-minute load is 4 or less before measuring (up to five minutes, then it runs and warns that the run is suspect).

meta.title: Benchmarks: every result, on the table · Pyreon
meta.description: Pyreon's benchmark record: real Chromium, production builds, medians with 95% confidence intervals and a correctness check before anything is timed. Every win, tie and loss.

hero.title: Every result, on the table.
hero.lede: Real Chromium, production builds, medians with 95% confidence intervals and a correctness check before anything is timed. The row board and the core scenarios run twice, and a win has to win both runs. Re-measured 2026-11-25 with Solid 2.0 stable and Vue's Vapor release candidate on the board beside Solid 1.9 and Vue 3, and published as measured, including what got worse; the bundle is from 2026-11-24 and sections not re-run keep their 2026-11-05 figures. Every number on every Pyreon page comes from here.
